messages.content: 你能幫我找到紐約有閱讀室和小說區的公共圖書館，然後在洛杉磯有Wi-Fi和有兒童區的公共圖書館，最後在芝加哥有咖啡廳和閱讀室的公共圖書館嗎？

function.name: public_library_find_nearby
function.description: Locate nearby public libraries based on specific criteria like English fiction availability and Wi-Fi. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The city and state, e.g. Boston, MA

facilities.description: Facilities and sections in public library.

message.reasoning:
The user wants to find public libraries in three cities with certain facilities:

1. New York (NY) - reading room and fiction section.
2. Los Angeles (LA) - Wi-Fi and children's section.
3. Chicago (IL) - cafe and reading room.

We need to call the function `public_library_find_nearby` for each location with appropriate facilities. The function expects a single argument object with keys: location (string), facilities (one of the enumerated strings). But the facilities parameter seems to accept only one value? It says type: "Wi-Fi" | "Reading Room" | "Fiction" | "Children Section" | "Cafe"[]; That suggests it can be an array? Actually the type shows "Cafe"[], maybe it's an array of strings? The description: "Facilities and sections in public library." So we might pass an array of desired facilities. But the type signature indicates union of string or array? It's ambiguous. We should pass an array of strings: ["Reading Room", "Fiction"] etc.

But the function signature: `_:{ location: string, facilities: "Wi-Fi" | "Reading Room" | "Fiction" | "Children Section" | "Cafe"[], }`. This means facilities can be either one of those strings or an array of "Cafe"? Wait "Cafe"[] means array of Cafe? Actually "Cafe"[] means array of strings "Cafe"? Might be mis-specified. We'll assume we can pass an array of strings.

Thus we will call the function thrice.

We need to produce calls in JSON format as per instructions. Each call must be separate. Then after receiving results, we will respond with the combined list.

We need to output calls in JSON format. According to guidelines: "When calling a tool, you must do so in JSON format. Do not wrap your JSON in markdown tags."

So we need to output something like:

{
"name":"public_library_find_nearby",
"arguments":{
    "location":"New York, NY",
    "facilities":["Reading Room","Fiction"]
}
}

Then next call etc.

We need to make sure we don't include extraneous text. Just the JSON. After all calls, we will combine results.

Let's proceed.
